A Niederlassungsleitung user's Quotations list only shows quotations
  belonging to their own Niederlassung (branch), regardless of what other
  branches' quotations exist in the system. This is deliberately end-to-end
  (real login, real list view) rather than a duplicate of the existing
  ORM-level unit tests covering the same scoping rule.

description:
A contact person filed under a customer may keep their own postal address
  instead of the customer's. This is deliberately end-to-end rather than a
  duplicate of the ORM-level unit tests covering the same rules: Odoo hides
  the address block on a Kontakt and only the "Eigene Adresse verwenden"
  switch reveals it, which no Python test can observe, and the decoupling
  has to hold through a real form save — the address synchronisation runs on
  a write the form composes, not one a test hands it.

description:
A correction that is not an absence (a transfer from another Niederlassung,
  say) has no native Odoo record: an allocation cannot be negative and a leave
  would show up as an absence. HR books it as an Anpassung directly in the
  Abwesenheitshistorie, with a mandatory reason, and the running Gesamt takes
  it into account immediately. This is deliberately end-to-end: the editable
  grid, the validation dialog and the recomputed Gesamt are OWL list behaviour
  no unit test can observe.

description:
A planner may assign any active employee of the company to a shift, but the
  Ressourcen dialog still opens on their own team so the everyday list stays
  short; reaching the rest of the company is a deliberate act.

  End-to-end because the behaviour under test is a rendered search state, not a
  computed set. Which employees the planner may assign is already proven at the
  unit level by test_planning_company_wide_assignment; what no TransactionCase
  can observe is that the dialog opens with the Mein Team facet applied, that
  removing it is what widens the visible list, and that a name from the widened
  list is selectable and lands on the form. That is AC-1 and AC-2.

  It deliberately stops at the form. Saving is covered by
  test_planning_company_wide_assignment, including the part a browser test
  would have to stage an Objekt for: a shift for somebody outside your team on
  a project that is not yours is refused by rule_planning_slot_global_scope,
  so "it saves" is two rules interacting rather than one rendering.

description:

  KWP workshop of 2026-09-09), walked through in her own name.

  Projekt overview and the Gantt rows the scope rules leave her, the buttons
  the matrix grants (Plan erstellen, the trash icon, Genehmigen) and the ones
  it withholds, and the pickers of the shift dialog. The rules themselves are
  proven at unit level (test_ifms_roles, test_planning_company_wide_assignment,
  test_self_planning, test_time_off_scope); this feature checks the rendered

  7) is already covered by company_wide_assignment.feature and is not repeated.

description:
A project without a customer must stay editable and savable, while a project
  that names one still cannot be saved without its Objekt. This is deliberately
  end-to-end because the defect lived entirely in the client's modifier
  evaluation: the Objekt was required unconditionally while Odoo hid the Kunde
  field on a project that is neither billable nor field-service, so the form
  demanded a value with no reachable source. The ORM never blocked it — the
  constraint has always exempted customer-less projects — so no TransactionCase
  can reproduce the failure. The unit tests in test_project_property.py assert
  the modifiers that reach the client; only a browser proves the record saves.

description:
A Bereichsleiterin opens a task and sees, as a stat button, how many
  timesheet entries on it still need her release; clicking it opens exactly
  those entries, where she validates them. This is deliberately end-to-end for
  two reasons the unit level cannot reach. First, the button has to survive
  view combination: project.view_task_form2 is inherited by hr_timesheet,
  project_enterprise, timesheet_grid and this module, and an arch assertion
  proves only that the xpath applied, not that the button rendered in the
  assembled form. Second, this is an access rule as the user experiences it —
  before #324 a Bereichsleiterin could not see her team's entries at all, so
  the number she gets after a real login is the behaviour under test.
  The counting rules themselves (validated, absence and public-holiday
  exclusion, the project rollup, the action domains) are unit tests in
  wolfinne_ifms_customization/tests/test_timesheet_validation_indicator.py, and
  the record rule in wolfinne_ifms_access/tests/test_timesheet_scope.py — none
  of that is re-proven here. The absence/public-holiday exclusion in particular
  cannot be set up from a browser at all: project_timesheet_holidays refuses to
  let a non-superuser create or modify a leave-linked timesheet line
  (_check_can_create / _check_can_write), so that case belongs to the unit
  level by construction.
